title: Oil shock meets a live G10 tightening cycle

topMovers.label: Brent intraweek
topMovers.cause: Four-month high on Hormuz and Red Sea disruption before a fade toward $106.

topMovers.label: Chokepoints disrupted
topMovers.cause: World Monitor’s board had Hormuz and Kerch as the hottest scores.

topMovers.label: US headline CPI
topMovers.cause: August in line; core +0.3% m/m vs 0.2% expected kept a September hike live.

topMovers.label: US diesel
topMovers.cause: Distillates, not WTI ticks, are the inflation path into food and freight.

topMovers.label: FOMC hike odds
topMovers.cause: Warsh tone plus the jobs beat pushed FedWatch into the 80s for 16 Sep.

energy.summary: Base of the week is a war premium on crude and a record-ish diesel print, with European gas storage poor for the date. Nat gas on World Monitor’s 9 Sep pulse was the weak sleeve (−1.2%), which is a US-hub story, not Europe. Distillates and chokepoints matter more than WTI ticks.
bullets: Brent tagged near $110 intraweek, then faded toward $106.
US diesel printed above $6/gallon on the morning wires.
European gas storage is tight into winter; US hub gas is the soft sleeve.

ai.summary: World Monitor’s tech sibling exists for infra mapping. No model-release or power-cap event dominated the geopolitics dashboard this week. Power and diesel for data centers are the cascade from energy, not the other way around — yet.
cascadingImpacts: Energy tax → power cost → AI infra pace
bullets: No verified model-release headline on the geopolitics board.
Constraint is power and diesel, not ideas.

war.summary: US–Iran at sea, Houthis opening a Yemen port front, Ukraine still the highest instability score on the board (UA 84). Nuclear-risk explainers are back in the OSINT stream. This is the constraint set for oil, grain, and insurance — not a separate geopolitics column.
cascadingImpacts: US–Iran + Houthis → Hormuz/Red Sea → insurance and ships
bullets: IRGC strikes on shipping in Hormuz; Houthis holding Mocha.
Yemen violence wired back into the US–Iran war.
Ukraine remains the highest instability score (UA 84).

food.summary: No new FAO-grade print in this week’s public tape. Transmission path is freight + diesel + Black Sea/Red Sea insurance, not a harvest headline. Keep the domain on the page so a quiet week stays visible.
cascadingImpacts: Diesel + insurance → food inflation with a lag
bullets: No harvest headline moved the public tape.
Quiet week still belongs on the page.

transport.summary: Civil and military aviation layers on the dashboard are the other half of the same corridor story as the ships. Delayed boxes and war-risk premia sit on the same map as Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb, and Suez.
cascadingImpacts: Chokepoints → ships and aviation → delayed boxes
bullets: Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb, and Suez all scored disrupted.
Aviation layers track the same corridor as maritime risk.

logistics.summary: Tanker risk, refined-product cracks, and 7 of 13 chokepoints disrupted. That is ships, war-risk premia, and delayed boxes — then food and diesel. Logistics is the wire between war and the CPI print.
cascadingImpacts: Tanker risk → refined cracks → freight inflation
bullets: 7 of 13 chokepoints disrupted on the public board.
Hormuz and Kerch posted the hottest scores.

demographics.summary: No new UN or major census print this week. Labor only showed up as the US jobs beat that helped reprice the Fed. Structural ageing and migration stay in the 2y/5y box until a print moves.
cascadingImpacts: Jobs beat → Fed odds → front-end yields
bullets: August payrolls +162k vs ~55k expected; unemployment 4.1%.
Ageing and migration stay in the longer horizons until a print moves.

public_policy.summary: FOMC 15–16 Sep is the event. ECB already hiked (second of 2026); BoJ is live 18 Sep. G10 tightening into an oil shock is the policy regime. Chair Warsh’s Jackson Hole tone plus the jobs beat had already lifted September odds; CPI pushed FedWatch into the 80s for +25 bp.
cascadingImpacts: CPI + Warsh tone → FOMC path → front-end yields · dollar
bullets: Fed funds still 3.50–3.75% after a year of holds.
Headline CPI +0.4% m/m, +3.4% y/y; core +2.4% y/y.
JPMorgan desk color: eight of nine DM central banks hike by year-end.

natural_resources.summary: Gold firm on the geopolitical bid and real-yield fight. Copper soft on the 9 Sep pulse. Stockpile and extraction data were not in the public World Monitor panels used for this dry run — flag for Pro / commodity sibling next Sunday. Mining-tech: no verified process breakthrough this week.
cascadingImpacts: War bid → gold · copper offered → mineral-security capex
bullets: Gold held the $4,300–4,400 area.
Copper was offered on the 9 Sep pulse.
Public dashboard did not yield a clean inventory series.

base: Oil stays three digits while the Strait is contested.
Risk assets chop after the Friday bounce.
risks: A hold after 80%+ odds — front-end rally, dollar dip, Warsh credibility hit.
Hormuz closed for more than a news cycle — diesel and Europe gas, not just Brent.
Equities treat an in-line headline as the cascade. It is not.

base: Oil war premium fades only if a ceasefire or a secure corridor appears.
Core inflation does not make a clean run at 2%.
Growth slows from the energy tax, not a 2020-style collapse.
risks: Second-round inflation in services if diesel and food stick.
Europe winter gas if storage and LNG routing stay ugly.
Policy error either way — too slow on headline, too fast on labor.

base: 2026 oil/war shock remembered as a mid-cycle supply break.
Policy stays higher for longer than the 2025 narrative wanted.
Capex gravitates to energy, grids, and secured minerals.
AI infra remains power-constrained, not idea-constrained.
risks: A real recession if tightening and oil run together.
A frozen conflict that institutionalizes $80–110 oil as the normal band.
Trade rewires around the Cape for years, not weeks.

base: Chokepoint politics and mineral security become standing features.
Demographics and public debt cap any 1970s policy replay.
Mining and refining capacity, not ore in the ground, set the resource constraint.
risks: A wider great-power war that takes the dashboard off monitor.
A clean peace plus productivity burst that collapses the war premium.
This brief would then look hawkish in hindsight.

cascadingImpacts: War → chokepoints → crude/diesel → headline CPI · inflation expectations → FOMC/ECB/BoJ path
Policy path → front-end yields · dollar → freight and food inflation with a lag
